boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Grimball's Landing record (July 16, 1863) in Operations Against the Defenses of Charleston [April-September 1863]. Terry's landing on James Island on July 8 and withdrawal on July 16-17 are context. Campaign-wide marches, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force text and the live page read 6,800 total (US 3,800; CS 3,000). Gillmore gives Terry's command as about 3,800 men and says Terry was attacked by a largely superior force. Jones says Terry had a larger force than the Confederates on James Island, gives Colquitt's column as about fourteen hundred, Way's as about eight hundred and Radcliffe's as about four hundred, and earlier says Terry outnumbered all of Beauregard's infantry in South Carolina.
claims.rationale: Gillmore's 3,800 matches the frozen US figure; the Confederate column figures are Jones's and sum to about 2,600, not an inspected total. Gillmore and Jones disagree on which side was larger. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Inconclusive and the live result Indecisive. Gillmore says the enemy was repulsed and Terry's command withdrawn on the 17th, its purpose accomplished; Jones says the Confederates retired with their object accomplished and that Terry abandoned the island that night, which was the desired result.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

open_questions: Terry's, Hagood's, Colquitt's and the signal officer's reports (listed for Grimball's Landing, p.581), the naval reports on the Pawnee and any returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (NPS battle page and frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Quincy A. Gillmore's report dated February 28, 1864 (Official Records I, XXVIII part 1, No. 2) is one family of interested Union accounts. Samuel Jones's The Siege of Charleston (1911) is a posthumous Confederate general's history that quotes Gillmore's, Seymour's, Strong's, Ripley's, Taliaferro's and Beauregard's reports and is not independent of them. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
